name: Inception
notes: Watched on 4K OLED. The spinning totem scene at the end still raises goosebumps.
review: A masterwork of original concept, non-linear pacing, and Hans Zimmer's iconic brass score. One of the greatest cinematic achievements of the 21st century.

name: Interstellar
notes: The docking scene ('No, it's necessary') is unmatched tension.
review: Transfers hard astrophysics into a tear-jerking examination of parental love transcending time and gravity.

name: The Dark Knight
notes: Heath Ledger's performance is transcendent. Every line has cultural weight.
review: Transformed comic-book cinema into a serious morality crime epic. Unquestionably peerless.

name: Dune: Part Two
notes: Saw it in IMAX 70mm. The sand-worm riding sequence shook the entire theater.
review: A grand sci-fi spectacle on par with Lawrence of Arabia and The Empire Strikes Back.

name: Blade Runner 2049
notes: Roger Deakins' cinematography is pure art. Colors are hypnotic.
review: A contemplative, slow-burn inquiry into humanity, memories, and soul.

name: Oppenheimer
notes: Cillian Murphy conveys so much tension through his eyes alone. The Trinity test sequence was terrifying silence.
review: Relentless tempo and sound design that portrays the burden of Prometheus.

name: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse
notes: Gwen's dimension watercolor art changing based on her emotions is genius.
review: Revolutionary animation language. Every single frame is a work of museum-worthy gallery art.

name: Whiplash
notes: J.K. Simmons gives an electrifying, terrifying performance. The finale Caravan drum solo is unmatched adrenaline.
review: A thrill ride disguised as a music drama that examines the fine line between greatness and madness.

name: Alien: Romulus
notes: Planned for weekend horror movie night.

name: Spirited Away
notes: Studio Ghibli's magnum opus. Joe Hisaishi's score touches the soul.
review: A timeless journey of resilience, wonder, and memory.
